record.original_question: Suppose a closed manifold (M, g) admits a non-zero (1, 1)-tensor field that is self-adjoint with respect to g, parallel and nilpotent.

evidence.quote: Suppose a closed manifold (M, g) admits a non-zero (1, 1)-tensor field that is self-adjoint with respect to g, parallel and nilpotent.

artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a list of open problems on geodesics by Burns and Matveev. Local existence of parallel self-adjoint nilpotent endomorphisms on pseudo-Riemannian manifolds is known (Boubel and others), and there is recent work on Nijenhuis geometry of parallel tensors and on cones over pseudo-Riemannian manifolds with parallel symmetric 2-tensors that splits into nilpotent/decomposable/complex-Riemannian cases. However, no source found definitively settles the global existence/classification question on closed manifolds, so the status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and questions about geodesics — Burns, Matveev
status_evidence.snippet: Problem list including reconstructing metrics from geodesics and questions about parallel self-adjoint tensors on closed manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed in a problem collection on geodesics, indicating it was posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On the algebra of parallel endomorphisms of a pseudo-Riemannian metric (Boubel)
status_evidence.snippet: For any self-adjoint nilpotent element N ... the set of germs of metrics such that {N} is in the algebra of parallel endomorphisms is non-empty.
status_evidence.claim: Local examples of parallel self-adjoint nilpotent endomorphisms exist in pseudo-Riemannian signature.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis geometry of parallel tensors
status_evidence.snippet: Analytical/geometric characterizations of integrability for nilpotent (1,1)-tensors among others.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies parallel nilpotent (1,1)-tensors but does not appear to settle the closed-manifold case.
